Journey production-certification casebook

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Separate contract completeness from go-live
  • Assemble tenant/journey/version evidence
  • Explain expiring certification

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Platform conformance
  2. 02Tenant configuration
  3. 03Live-provider certification
  4. 04UAT + migration
  5. 05Security + DR
  6. 06Independent approvals
  7. 07Production admission + expiry monitoring

1. Platform evidence

Contract, schemas, persistent APIs, lifecycle composition, exact accounting, workspaces and generated conformance establish the internal platform boundary for the current template version.

2. Tenant evidence

The regulated entity must approve product/policy, pricing, content, roles, delegations, providers, accounting mappings, reports, procedures and risk acceptance. Journey UAT must cover happy and adverse cases with the tenant's actual configuration.

3. Live operations

Provider contracts/credentials, India residency, callback/reconciliation certification, capacity/SLO, support/on-call, migration, backup/restore, failover/failback, security tests and institution-witnessed exercises must be current.

4. Decision

Production-ready is tenant-, environment-, journey-, configuration- and version-specific.

The contract requires eleven current evidence domains plus every provider family declared by the template.

The API rejects production proposals until trusted provider, deployment and institution registries are joined; request-body references cannot certify a journey.

A changed or suspended dependency reopens certification.
